note: The reference platform's oracle: which cells (account × endpoint × resource) must produce a finding under each combination of flags. Written by hand from the access model rather than taken from the tool's output: a reference generated by the program under test tests it for consistency with itself. There are 28 combinations, not 4096: the flags touch non-intersecting sets of cells — except for one pair — so they are tested one at a time, in pairs where an intersection is plausible, and all together. The claim of orthogonality is tested by the verification itself: in `all-eight` the matrix discrepancies must match the union of the single combinations, and the findings by body must match `list-no-filter`.
cellKey: account + endpoint + resource; resource = null on endpoints with no path parameters

POLYGON_DEFECT_CROSS_TENANT.title: No tenant filter in GET /v1/orders/{orderId} for the brand accounts: a resource of a foreign tenant is served 200 instead of 403
POLYGON_DEFECT_CROSS_TENANT.note: No tenant filter in GET /v1/orders/{orderId} for the brand accounts: a resource of a foreign tenant is served 200 instead of 403. Hits 10 cells — two foreign orders for each of the five brand accounts. The anonymous account is not hit: authentication is checked before authorization. The holding and affiliate accounts are not hit: each has an order authorization branch of its own.

POLYGON_DEFECT_NO_ROLE_CHECK.title: The role is not checked in GET /v1/admin/accounts: any non-administrator gets 200 instead of 403
POLYGON_DEFECT_NO_ROLE_CHECK.note: The role is not checked in GET /v1/admin/accounts: any non-administrator gets 200 instead of 403. Hits 7 cells — the four users of both brands, the holding account, the affiliate and support over two brands. The administrator gets 200 without the defect too, the anonymous account still gets 401. The affiliate and support each added a cell here, because both are just as much non-administrators; this is the only place where either of these accounts hit a previous flag, and the previous cells stayed as they were all the same.

POLYGON_DEFECT_IDOR_SAME_TENANT.title: IDOR inside a tenant in GET /v1/orders/{orderId}: another user's order in one's own tenant is served 200 instead of 403
POLYGON_DEFECT_IDOR_SAME_TENANT.note: IDOR inside a tenant in GET /v1/orders/{orderId}: another user's order in one's own tenant is served 200 instead of 403. Hits 4 cells. It does not hit the administrator: the resources of its own tenant are meant for it by policy, and it gets 200 in any mode. It does not hit the holding and affiliate accounts: neither of them has its own tenant among the orders.

POLYGON_DEFECT_LIST_NO_FILTER.title: No tenant filter in the brand list GET /v1/orders: the orders of all tenants are served
POLYGON_DEFECT_LIST_NO_FILTER.note: No tenant filter in the brand list GET /v1/orders: the orders of all tenants are served. The status does not change — 200 both with the defect and without it — so the defect is visible only through a signal over the body (ADR-0011). Hits 6 pairs: the three accounts of tenant-a (alice-a, bob-a, admin-a) against the two accounts of tenant-b (carol-b, dave-b). The anonymous account gets 401 and does not enter the comparison. The holding rollup is not hit by this flag — it is a different query — and never lands in a pair: its rows carry the brand, so its body does not match a brand one in any mode. The affiliate does not enter the pairs at all: the order list is closed to it (403), there is no body. Support over two brands does not enter for two reasons at once: its list is a different query, untouched by this flag, and there is nobody to compare it against, because it shares a tenant with every brand account and kinship with the holding one.

POLYGON_DEFECT_CROSS_HOLDING.title: The holding rollup is not limited to its own subtree: GET /v1/orders/{orderId} serves the holding a resource of a brand of a foreign holding — 200 instead of 403
POLYGON_DEFECT_CROSS_HOLDING.note: The holding rollup is not limited to its own subtree: GET /v1/orders/{orderId} serves the holding a resource of a brand of a foreign holding — 200 instead of 403. Hits 2 cells: helen-h1 against the two orders of tenant-b. This is exactly the defect that was inexpressible before ADR-0013: attributing the holding to its own brand forced a rule with scope: foreign-tenant to be declared, and that opened access to the foreign holding as well.

POLYGON_DEFECT_ANCESTOR_LEAK.title: The visibility of the summary statements is disclosed up the tree instead of down, and along the WHOLE chain of ancestors: GET /v1/statements/{statementId} serves an account the statement of any tenant standing above it
POLYGON_DEFECT_ANCESTOR_LEAK.note: The visibility of the summary statements is disclosed up the tree instead of down, and along the WHOLE chain of ancestors: GET /v1/statements/{statementId} serves an account the statement of any tenant standing above it. Hits 6 cells: alice-a, bob-a and admin-a against the statement of their holding, ivan-af1 against both statements at once — the brand's (one step) and the holding's (two steps) — plus sara-ac against the holding-1 statement, which stands above its membership in tenant-a. The role has nothing to do with it — the brand's admin is hit exactly like its users, because the defect is in the relation to the resource, not in the role check. It does not hit carol-b and dave-b: holding-1 is not their ancestor. It does not hit helen-h1: the statement of its tenant and the statement of its brand are meant for it on a correct platform too.

POLYGON_DEFECT_PARENT_LEAK.title: The same upward disclosure, but exactly ONE level: the platform asks "a statement of my tenant or of my parent?" instead of walking the tree — the typical implementation through a denormalized "parent tenant" field in the token
POLYGON_DEFECT_PARENT_LEAK.note: The same upward disclosure, but exactly ONE level: the platform asks "a statement of my tenant or of my parent?" instead of walking the tree — the typical implementation through a denormalized "parent tenant" field in the token. Hits 5 cells: the same three brand ones as ANCESTOR_LEAK, plus ivan-af1 against the statement of its brand and sara-ac against the holding-1 statement — that one is exactly one step above its membership in tenant-a, so both flags give this cell alike. It does not hit the cell ivan-af1 × statement-h1-0001 — from there the holding is two steps away — and the whole difference between the two flags lives in that one cell. On a two-level tree it does not exist, and the defects are indistinguishable; the third level was added to the tree for the sake of its appearance.

POLYGON_DEFECT_PRIMARY_TENANT_ONLY.title: The account's set of memberships is collapsed to the first tenant: GET /v1/orders/{orderId} serves support over two brands the first brand only and denies the second with 403 where access is declared to be granted
POLYGON_DEFECT_PRIMARY_TENANT_ONLY.note: The account's set of memberships is collapsed to the first tenant: the token carries a single "tenant" field because every account used to have one tenant. Hits 2 cells: sara-ac against the two orders of tenant-b. The only defect of the polygon that shows itself as a denial rather than as excess access — kind: unexpected-denial. Before ADR-0017 it would have been indistinguishable from correct behaviour: there was nothing to declare the second brand one's own with, and a denial on it would have agreed with the expectation. The other accounts are not hit — only one of them has a set of memberships.

POLYGON_DEFECT_GEO_BYPASS.title: The jurisdiction of the request is not checked: GET /v1/orders and GET /v1/orders/{orderId} are served from a prohibited country too — 200 instead of 451
POLYGON_DEFECT_GEO_BYPASS.note: The jurisdiction of the request is not checked: orders are served even when the request is tagged with a country from the prohibition (the cf-ipcountry header from the CDN). The only defect of the polygon that is not expressible through permissions: the role, the tenant and the resource in these cells are the same as in the base conditions, and "alice-a × her own order" lawfully gives 200 without the tag and must give a denial with it. They can be told apart only by declaring the request conditions as a separate dimension (ADR-0019). Hits 19 cells under the geo-blocked conditions: seven on the list (everyone the list is meant for: the four users, the administrator, the holding and support) and twelve on the resources (one own order for each of the four users, the two of tenant-a for the administrator, its two brands for the holding, all four for support over two brands). Orders are not meant for the affiliate under any conditions — 403 — and it produces no cells; the anonymous account gets 401. A correct platform answers 451, and that is a denial, not a failure: see ADR-0019.

POLYGON_DEFECT_SCOPE_ALL_HONORED.title: A hidden query parameter widens the listing: ?scope=all removes the tenant filter in the brand list GET /v1/orders
POLYGON_DEFECT_SCOPE_ALL_HONORED.note: A hidden query parameter removes the tenant filter: the filter is there, but it is switched off by a context attribute. It differs from POLYGON_DEFECT_LIST_NO_FILTER both in mechanics and in the set of cells: that one is visible on base requests, this one only under the conditions where the parameter is declared (wide-scope), and on base requests it does not show at all. The status does not change — 200 both with the defect and without — so it is visible only through a signal over the body. Hits the same 6 pairs as list-no-filter, but in different cells: the three accounts of tenant-a against the two accounts of tenant-b, all under the wide-scope conditions. The holding and support are not hit: they have listing branches of their own, the parameter does not reach them, and their bodies keep their attribution by brand. The list is closed to the affiliate (403), the anonymous account gets 401. The conditions with a query parameter were introduced on the polygon for the sake of this flag: an attribute in the query string travels a different path than a header — through the building of the address — and without such a cell the claim "the parameter reaches the platform" would rest on a single unit test.

POLYGON_DEFECT_WRITE_CROSS_TENANT.title: No tenant filter on a write: POST /v1/orders/{orderId}/cancel cancels an order of another tenant instead of refusing — 200 instead of 403
POLYGON_DEFECT_WRITE_CROSS_TENANT.note: No tenant filter on a write. A mirror of POLYGON_DEFECT_CROSS_TENANT on POST, and it affects the same 10 cells: two foreign orders for each of the five brand accounts. What makes it worth having is not the branch in the code but the method: without it the whole write path of the tool — the --unsafe-methods flag, the skip of write endpoints without it, writeMethodsProbed in the report — was not proved by a single cell. The holding is not affected in either direction: reading a rollup of its brands is allowed to it, cancelling their orders is not, and the platform refuses it in every mode. The affiliate is refused as well; the anonymous account gets 401.

POLYGON_DEFECT_WRITE_NO_OWNER_CHECK.title: No owner check on a write: a player cancels a neighbour's order inside their own tenant — 200 instead of 403
POLYGON_DEFECT_WRITE_NO_OWNER_CHECK.note: No owner check on a write, the counterpart of POLYGON_DEFECT_IDOR_SAME_TENANT. Affects 4 cells: each of the four players against the order of their neighbour in the same tenant. The administrator is not affected — everything inside the tenant is allowed to them in any mode. On a real platform this is the more expensive of the two: reading someone else's order leaks data, cancelling it takes money away from them.

variants.note: The defect is visible twice: in the base conditions and in the declared wide-scope ones — the brand branch serves everything in both cases, the parameter has nothing to do with it. This follows from conditions being a dimension, and it is not an error: from the outside "a leak with the parameter" and "a leak without it" may be different paths in the code, and the tool does not tell them apart. The price is two defect groups for one breakage of the platform; the reader of the report is told about this in docs/report.md: two groups that differ only by their conditions are most likely one.

The request conditions as a dimension of the matrix. In the correct mode the same cells give 451 — a denial for legal reasons — and there are no findings; from which it also follows that not one previous combination is touched by this flag: without it the geo cells answer 451 under any other defects.

The first variant that runs with --unsafe-methods. Without the flag orders.cancel is skipped and the report says so; with it the same matrix machinery walks it, and a write cell turns out to be an ordinary cell whose method changes state.

The write counterpart of idor-same-tenant. The sets of cells of the two write defects do not intersect, for the same reason the read ones do not: one lives on foreign tenants, the other inside one's own.

The conditions with a query parameter. There are no matrix discrepancies and there must not be: the parameter by itself neither grants nor takes away permissions, and the outcome stays as it was. What breaks is the content of the response, and that is visible only by comparing bodies within one and the same set of conditions — the pair "a base request against a request with the parameter" is deliberately not compared, two variables would change there at once (ADR-0019).

All nine defects at once. The findings must be a union: the discrepancies of the base conditions — the same as in all-eight, cell for cell — plus the same defects seen under the geo-blocked conditions. The claim of orthogonality is tested right here: the conditions change not one base cell, while the geo cells repeat the picture of permissions, because with the geo barrier removed the same authorization runs. There is one exception, and a substantive one: the collapsed set of memberships is visible in the base conditions as a denial (unexpected-denial on sara-ac), and under the geo conditions it is not visible at all — there a denial is the declared expectation.

All ten defects at once, and the picture is identical to all-nine — cell for cell, 82 findings against 82. This is a claim, not a coincidence: the tenth defect, the hidden `?scope=all`, removes the tenant filter from the brand list, and with `list-no-filter` on there is no filter there any more — nothing left to remove. A defect invisible in the presence of another one is a normal thing, and it is worth having it visible as a number rather than as an argument. The six wide-scope pairs that `scope-all` produces on its own are already present in all-nine, produced there by `list-no-filter`.
Both write defects at once. The findings must be the union, 14 cells: the sets do not intersect, and that is the claim being checked, not an observation about the implementation.
